about.label: A little bit about me
about.paragraph1: I've been a designer for 14 years, transitioning into the digital world seven years ago. Throughout my career, I've worked with major companies across diverse industries and I am currently a Senior Product Designer open to new opportunities.
about.paragraph2: What drives me most is the ability to streamline processes and craft meaningful experiences through functional, visually compelling interfaces. I thrive on bridging strategy and execution, collaborating closely with cross-functional teams to turn complex challenges into intuitive solutions — always with a strong focus on business impact and user needs.

hero.label: Digital menu - iFood
hero.headline: A Progressive Web App for food delivery. It's one of the products of the iFood ecosystem.

challenge.title: Challenge
challenge.leftParagraph1: The Digital Menu is a product designed to enable restaurants to leverage iFood's technology and logistics infrastructure to promote their business and products autonomously.
challenge.leftParagraph2: Since it was a new product, we faced the challenge of understanding both the restaurant market and customer behavior.
challenge.leftIntro: I was involved in all stages of the process, including:
leftItems: Creating landing pages to promote the product
Running conversion tests on landing pages
Designing the product itself, including purchase and payment flows
Designing the configuration portal, where restaurant owners set up their digital menu
Conducting qualitative and quantitative research (with over 13k respondents) to understand adoption challenges.
challenge.rightParagraph1: Every quarter, we analyzed product adoption impacts based on our strategic efforts and research. I played a key role in understanding the user journey, identifying needs and objections, and proposing improvements to enhance adoption metrics.
challenge.rightParagraph2: I joined the project before the product launch, and within just four months, the Digital Menu was already handling 400,000 orders per month. By the time I left the project, it was on a growth trajectory to reach 3 million orders by June 2022.

presentation.text: Due to confidentiality agreements, this project cannot be shared, but I can walk you through it in a live presentation.

hero.label: Compass - Nilo
hero.headline: Nilo Compass helps healthcare managers track key metrics with clear and reliable data.

challenge.label: Challenge
challenge.p1: Hospital managers and, especially, health plan administrators need to constantly track key metrics to make informed decisions with autonomy.
challenge.p2: However, management reports are often ineffective when they lack reliable data or fail to provide actionable insights for operational monitoring. Additionally, we noticed that managers often requested data without a clear understanding of why they needed it.
challenge.p3: With this in mind, we developed Nilo Analytics, a platform where all insights were shaped directly from user needs, identified through design thinking and co-creation sessions.
challenge.p4: Our main goal was not only to provide access to data but to ensure that managers received truly relevant indicators - not just what they thought they needed, but what was actually valuable for their business and operations, empowering them to make strategic decisions with confidence.
challenge.p5: To achieve this, I conducted an in-depth study of key metrics, allowing me to define and suggest the most meaningful insights in a way that was both simple to consume and strategically useful.

myRole.label: My Contribution
myRole.p1: Together with the PM of the project, I understood the business needs and goals for this new product. After this step I led sessions of co-creation with potential users, to understand their needs.
myRole.p2: Later in this process, I did competitor analysis, UX and UI studies, prototypes, user tests and finally followed the implementation.

cocreation.title: Co-creation
cocreation.subtitle: Understanding pain points and users goals
cocreation.p1: Over several weeks, I worked with a group of managers and our Customer Success team to gain a holistic understanding of operational processes and managerial needs.
cocreation.p2: After structuring this research into clear documentation, we categorized the information into thematic pages, ensuring clarity and usability.

validation.title: Validation
validation.subtitle: Concepts and formulas
validation.p1: Another key challenge was standardizing all data types used in the project. We meticulously documented the concepts and formulas behind each indicator.
validation.p2: This comprehensive validation process became the foundation for the engineering team to build the data architecture.

uiDesign.label: UI Design
uiDesign.p1: Once the information architecture was validated, my focus shifted to transforming complex data into a simple and functional interface.
uiDesign.p2: I worked side by side with the engineering team, ensuring that every experience I designed was feasible to implement. This close collaboration allowed us to validate technical constraints early and refine solutions together.
uiDesign.p3: Leveraging the company's design system, I created new components tailored to this product's unique needs.
uiDesign.p4: The goal was to present high volumes of data in a way that is clear, visually appealing, and actionable, while ensuring that our design choices aligned with technical feasibility.
